limits: A valid receipt says each party’s key signed its own part and the parts chain. It does not say any party told the truth.

The carried keys are the parties’ only if the verifier already holds those key_ids from somewhere else. A receipt cannot vouch for its own keys. When two roles are signed by one key, one holder signed both.
The acceptance names who accepted. The signature proves the acceptor’s key signed the receipt, not that the person named did.
money none means no money is held or paid by this receipt.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a receipt that still verifies.
The checks prove only what they test. A passed record says the pinned commands exited 0 on that tree, not that the work is good.
A test that cannot fail is not detected by this record.

The checker ran them as recorded only as far as the verifier trusts the checker’s key. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued the record, and content_hash that it was not edited since; the carried key is the checker’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a record that still verifies.
A delivery says what the doer’s Tick recorded handing in, not that the work is right. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued it, and content_hash that it was not edited since.
cents marked reported came from the agent’s platform and were not measured.
It does not prove the order exists or that this delivery answers it; that is checked where a receipt binds the two.
The carried key is the doer’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else. A delivery cannot vouch for its own key.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a delivery that still verifies.
A work order says what was asked, not that anything was done. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued it, and content_hash that it was not edited since.
The carried key is the buyer’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else. A work order cannot vouch for its own key.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a work order that still verifies.
payment none means no money is held for this order.

order.what:
Finding F1 of NOTE-mvrnfs15 (decisions GD-82, GD-83): a release made by Tick must pass `tick landings`.

WHAT IS WRONG. `releaseGaps` in packages/cli/src/landings-check.ts reads `receipts/<version>.json` at the release commit (`facts.releaseReceipt`, which landings-command.ts feeds with `git show <sha>:receipts/<version>.json`). A receipt that names the release commit cannot be inside that commit, and `tick_release` commits only package.json, package-lock.json and releases/<version>.json. So every release Tick makes reads "a release made outside Tick" (seen on release 0.5.261, commit 97968f3eec0939382018681823110abf75fc654e, whose release task is 01a180cd-7221-743c-a3c0-c1e489b00987 in run 01a180cd-59b5-77f9-ac04-42f90ee977f5; its task output is {base, gated, commit: <the release commit>, pushed, shasum, tarball, version, record_sha256, tarball_sha256, gate_check_sha256, gate_summary_sha256}, task type "release"). The coordinator DOES sign a release receipt for that task: GET /v1/runs/:id/tasks/:taskId/release-receipt, `HttpCoordinatorClient.getTaskReleaseReceipt(runId, taskId)` (already used by `tick export --form release-receipt` in export-command.ts), schema tick.release-receipt.v1, with `release.commit` = the release commit and `release.version`. `verifyDocument` of packages/verify reads it as kind "release-receipt", valid.

THE CHANGE. For a commit classified as a release, find, in the coordinator's runs (the `getRuns` that `checkCommits` already takes), the task of type "release" whose `output.commit` equals the commit's sha, the way `taskOf` finds a land task by `output.sha`. If one is found, fetch its release receipt (a new OPTIONAL member of `Facts`, like `receiptText`, fed in landings-command.ts from an optional `getTaskReleaseReceipt?` of `LandingsClient`; a client that cannot ask says so as a gap, as `receiptText` does), verify it offline with `facts.verify`, and require kind "release-receipt", valid, `release.commit` equal to the sha and `release.version` equal to the version in the subject. Any failure is a gap that says which. If no release task names the commit, the existing git path (`facts.releaseReceipt`) stays exactly as it is, and with neither the gap is OUTSIDE_TICK (keep its wording) followed by the runs' `problems`, as a landing does. Do not read the runs for a commit that is not a release.

CONSTRAINTS. packages/cli/src/landings-command.test.ts is exactly 500 lines and cannot grow; tests of the new behavior go in a NEW file packages/cli/src/landings-release.test.ts (under 500 lines, module comment 25 lines or fewer) built on packages/cli/src/landings-check.test-support.ts (extend it if needed). Cover: a release whose task is found and whose receipt verifies is ok; no matching task and no git receipt is OUTSIDE_TICK; a receipt naming another commit; another version; a receipt that does not verify; a coordinator that refuses; a client that cannot ask; a different task of type "land" or "implement" with the same sha in its output is not taken for the release; the git fallback still passes. Each assertion must be able to fail: check by changing the code. The module comments of landings-check.ts and landings-command.ts may not grow; landings-command.ts's says "A release commit is a gap unless `receipts/<version>.json` at that commit verifies" and must say what is true after this change. Existing tests that encode the old behavior are edited only where this change breaks them, and the report lists them. A source file stays under 500 lines (landings-check.ts is 408, landings-command.ts 418). Touch no other file.
